content.content:
# @eltonbautista/vue

Cabinet is a small, playful Vue 3 component library with an arcade-cabinet feel and a tested accessibility contract on every component.

**Components:** `CabButton`, `CabTextField`, `CabCheckbox`, `CabSwitch`, `CabSelect`, `CabTabs`, `CabDialog`, `CabCard`.

## Install

```sh
npm i @eltonbautista/vue @eltonbautista/tokens
```

```ts
// main.ts
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/tokens.css'   // design tokens (CSS custom properties)
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/fonts.css'    // Sora + Outfit (optional)
import '@eltonbautista/vue/style.css'       // component styles
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabButton, CabTextField } from '@eltonbautista/vue'
const email = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <CabTextField v-model="email" label="Email" type="email" />
  <CabButton>Book a seat</CabButton>
</template>
```

## Accessibility

Every component follows a WAI-ARIA APG pattern and documents its keyboard map, focus behaviour and screen-reader output. Each one is tested in a real browser for keyboard interaction and axe violations. See the Storybook docs for each component's Accessibility section.

content.text:
The landing page is in `src/App.vue` and `npm run build` passes with no errors. I did not run it in a browser or run an accessibility audit, so the WCAG 2.2 AA and keyboard claims are based on the design system's documented behaviour and the markup I wrote, not on a test run.

**What's on the page**
- **Title and intro:** an h1 and a short intro paragraph.
- **Tracks:** three `CabCard`s linking to `/tracks/board`, `/tracks/digital` and `/tracks/larp`. The card's `href` stretches the link over the whole card, so clicking anywhere on it goes to the track page.
- **Sign-up form:** name, email and experience level (a `CabSelect`), plus a code-of-conduct `CabCheckbox`. The submit button stays disabled until the checkbox is ticked, and a visible hint linked to the button says why. Submitting validates the fields, moves focus to the first invalid one, and otherwise opens a confirmation dialog.
- **Booking confirmation:** the dialog summarises the details and says the seat is not booked until confirmed. Only its Confirm button makes the booking. Cancel closes it without booking, and the design system returns focus to the trigger.
- **Email reminders:** a `CabSwitch` that saves on change with no save button. A polite live region announces "Saving…" and then the result, and it rolls back if the save fails.

**Choices I made that you may want to change**
- The track blurbs and the intro copy are placeholder text I wrote.
- The booking and reminder saves are stubs. The booking resolves after a 300 ms delay and nothing is sent anywhere. Reminders are stored in `localStorage` under `workshop-email-reminders`. Replace both with real calls.
- There is no router in this app. The track links are plain anchors, so the `/tracks/*` pages must be served separately, or they will 404 under the Vite dev server.
- I didn't run `vue-tsc`, since the project doesn't have it and `vite build` doesn't type-check `.vue` files.

`npm run build` also created a `dist/` folder in the project, which wasn't there before. Nothing has been committed.
